builder_plan.scenario: Tool errors or unavailable services cause your agent to abandon recoverable tasks.
builder_plan.change: Inject repeatable tool failures and change only the recovery policy.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current retry and fallback behavior under the same injected failures.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Recovered tasks, duplicate side effects, retries, time to recovery, and total cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: EvoX: Rethinking the Agent Harness as a Runtime Policy
summary: EvoX replaces the implicit, prompt-only orchestration logic of conventional agent harnesses with a Rust-based runtime that deterministically enforces action realization, execution continuity, and outcome grounding alongside the model's own decisions. It costs an additional runtime layer (Rust service deployment and maintenance), constrains the harness to specific tool-call and verification semantics, and its gains are model-dependent, averaging only ~3 points overall. It can fail when tasks depend on memory or extensions the runtime deliberately omits, when its deterministic controls misjudge legitimate completion claims, or when a provider's API behavior diverges from the verified request patterns.
rationale: The modest average improvement and strong model dependence mean a constrained team should validate it on their own models and workloads before committing to replacing their existing harness.
technique: Runtime policy harness for LLM agents

claims.statement: EvoX replaces the implicit, prompt-only orchestration logic of conventional agent harnesses with a Rust-based runtime that deterministically enforces action realization, execution continuity, and outcome grounding alongside the model's own decisions. It costs an additional runtime layer (Rust service deployment and maintenance), constrains the harness to specific tool-call and verification semantics, and its gains are model-dependent, averaging only ~3 points overall. It can fail when tasks depend on memory or extensions the runtime deliberately omits, when its deterministic controls misjudge legitimate completion claims, or when a provider's API behavior diverges from the verified request patterns.

EvoX achieves a 56.2% success rate over 691 task-model pairs, about 3.0 percentage points above the average of five other harnesses, with larger model-dependent gains on GLM-5.3 (+10.7 points) and Kimi K3 (+7.9 points).
